_comment: The seven API routes, each with the gates its POST handler is expected to run before it
touches the request body or the network. A route on disk that is not named here fails:
a new endpoint must be written down by a person, not discovered by a scanner that then
has nothing to compare it against.
`gates` are asserted to appear EARLIER IN THE HANDLER than the first body read and any
outbound fetch. They are all plain early-returning `if`s in the source, with nothing
structural holding them in place, which is exactly why the ordering is pinned here.
`bodyCap` is true when the handler buffers a body and therefore needs its own
(API-ON-DROPLET.md:180) matches on a header that a chunked request simply omits, and
the runbook records that LimitRequestBody and RewriteRule are both inert behind
ProxyPass, so that directive is the only perimeter outside the handler.

routes.note: Issues an ALTCHA challenge. No body is read.

The one route that makes an outbound fetch. If any gate moves below `await request.text()` or below fetch(targetUrl), this endpoint becomes a free unauthenticated fetch proxy on the box that also serves the team's WordPress.
Reflects the caller's own address from headers. No body is read.
Mints a test id. No body is read.
Reads a JSON body carrying the test id.
Analytics counters. The first route to get an in-process body bound; the other three copied it.

DELIBERATELY has no origin gate: it is called with a bearer STATS_TOKEN by the owner and by ops tooling, not from a browser, so an Origin allowlist would only lock out curl. The rate limit still comes first, because a bearer check with no limit is a free brute-force target. An unset STATS_TOKEN makes the route 404.
